title: Month intervals land on the same day; month-end rolls back
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin (Settings Service), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). These are numeric/date-accuracy cases (Rule 116): seed the exact inputs, read the produced value back, and compare it to the stated value - never eyeball, never accept "a number".
  2. Two schedules to seed: a routine service with a 1-month calendar interval, and one with a 90-day interval, on assets you can complete on specific dates. Seed: Settings > Maintenance > New schedule; Add service with Every 1 month; a second with Every 90 days. Compute each expected date by hand first.
custom_steps:
1. Complete the 1-month service on 15 Jan 2026 and read the next due date; complete again on 15 Feb 2026 and read the next.
  2. Complete the 1-month service on 31 Jan 2026 and read the next due date, then the cycle after.
  3. Complete the 1-month service on 31 Jan 2028 (leap year) and read the next due date.
  4. Complete the 90-day service on 1 Jan 2026, then on 1 Feb 2026, comparing the day-of-month against the month version.
  5. Confirm the same due date shows on the asset Maintenance tab and the worklist row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month: 15 Jan 2026 -> 15 Feb 2026, and 15 Feb 2026 -> 15 Mar 2026.
  • Where the anchor day is missing in the target month it falls on that month's last day: 31 Jan 2026 + 1 month -> 28 Feb 2026 (next cycle counts from 28 Feb 2026 -> 28 Mar 2026); 31 Jan 2028 + 1 month -> 29 Feb 2028.
  • A days interval drifts: 90 days from 1 Jan 2026 -> 1 Apr 2026, but 90 days from 1 Feb 2026 -> 2 May 2026 (not the 1st).
  • The same computed due date shows identically on the asset Maintenance tab and the worklist row.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10559 (S2); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S2; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R14: “A months interval resolves to the same day of a later month, counted from the last completion, and produces a specific date rather than a month. A days interval counts days and drifts relative to the calendar”
  • S2-E5: “Where the anchor day does not exist in the target month, the date falls on that month's last day. A service completed on 31 January and set to one month comes due 28 February, and the following cycle counts from that date”
